name: Ebla
description: A star 29 parsecs away, the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114322: radius 1.027 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.404 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.055) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114322: effective temperature 4543 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.106)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 4.79 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 13 published values span log g 4.02 to 4.81, across which the limb law changes by at most 1.0% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114322: distance 28.726 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.007), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 29 parsecs away, the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 0.404 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,543 K, so 1.027 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 114322: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 218566
quotes.card: HD 218566 is a star in the equatorial zodiac constellation of Pisces.
quotes.introduction: It has the proper name Ebla, after a kingdom in ancient Syria.
